Leash checks on an ordinary phase
This section covers what is expected

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the operating rules for handling companion animal bookings, check-in, and in-flight care without delay or confusion.

Staff must verify carrier condition, labels, vaccination papers, and owner contact details before acceptance. Every handoff must be calm, exact, and recorded at once. If a traveler arrives unsettled, the shift coordinator must intervene quickly and keep the exchange respectful. Cabin staff must be told when an animal is loaded, moved, or observed to be distressed.

<<FACT F090>> During the same shift, the coordinator must ensure that any incident is escalated through the proper channel and that the record is complete before the desk closes. Staff must not improvise instructions or leave gaps in the chain of custody. If an animal shows signs of illness, escape risk, or injury, the traveler must be kept informed in plain language and the matter must move to the senior coordinator without hesitation.

<<FACT F091>> Bookings may not be accepted on verbal assurance alone. The desk must confirm eligibility, route constraints, and all required documents before confirmation is issued. If a traveler such as Zain Clark or Sara Shah presents special handling needs, the coordinator must flag the file, coordinate with cabin staff, and keep the tone firm but courteous. Teddy, if presented for transport, must be treated with the same care and attention as any other approved pet.

All staff must use prompt, respectful communication and maintain a steady pace under pressure. Any uncertainty must be raised immediately rather than guessed through. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty manager at once if the situation is unclear.
